clue.text: See 11
Bossy-boots consumed spring onion

indicators.note: the hyphenated phrase has eaten the answer, which sits inside its letters across the hyphen

explanation.surface: A domineering person has wolfed down a spring onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' tells you the answer is swallowed by Bossy-boots: bosSY-BOots. SYBO (also sybow) is a dialect word, chiefly Scottish, for a spring onion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybo is a Scottish and northern dialect name for the young green onion also called a scallion.

clue.text: Ataturk's officer horrified? No way!

indicators.note: no way means take away the abbreviation for a way or street from the word before

parts.note: horrified means aghast
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone aghast at an officer under Ataturk exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way!' reads as an exclamation, but it tells you to drop ST (street, a way) from AGHAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An agha was a title for a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire and Turkey.

clue.text: I love it out East around the Villa d'Este's town

indicators.note: around means the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
out means the letter for East is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A tourist gushes about the Italian town of the Villa d'Este.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E (East) from I LOVE IT, leaving ILOVIT; 'around' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tivoli, near Rome, is the hill town where the Renaissance Villa d'Este and its fountains stand.

clue.text: Harder schools failing an Oxonian postgraduate

indicators.note: failing schools are in a broken state, so their letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tougher schools fail to produce Oxford graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' is the anagram signal for HARDER SCHOOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhodes Scholar holds an international scholarship for postgraduate study at Oxford University.

clue.text: See 11 and 13
After-school activities could be

parts.note: read not as clubs after lessons but as gatherings of former pupils long after leaving school

explanation.surface: A remark about what children do after lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-boy and old-girl gatherings are events held by former pupils years after leaving school.

clue.text: Finished in a state between Scylla and Charybdis?

parts.note: finished means at an end
to be in a state is to be upset or angry

explanation.surface: A sailor finishes in a panic, caught between the two sea monsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Scylla and Charybdis were the twin monsters of the Odyssey's strait; to be between them is to be in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught between two deadly monsters is a picture of being in danger, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Virginia might be when full of remorse and wretchedness

definitions.text: Virginia might be when full of remorse
definitions.meaning: Virginia is a US state, and one feeling remorse would be apologetic

explanation.surface: An American state is sorry and wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of affairs that is pitiful and miserable is commonly called sorry; Virginia, a US state, feeling remorse fits too.

clue.text: See 13 down
Restore strikers with second legs

parts.note: to restore something is to return it
matches are struck to light them, so they are strikers

explanation.surface: Bring back the forwards for the second legs of the ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' suggests footballers, but it means matches you strike; a two-legged tie's second leg is the return match.
explanation.definitionFit: In football cup ties played home and away, the second leg is the return fixture.

clue.text: They're off after this stress, terror and rude conflict!

indicators.note: conflict means the letters fight and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A race start full of stress, fear and rude clashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' signals an anagram of STRESS, TERROR, AND and RUDE, all nineteen letters. Horse races begin with the starter's call: they're under starter's orders... and they're off!
explanation.definitionFit: Racing commentators say the horses are under the starter's command just before announcing that they're off.

clue.text: He portrayed Churchill as vigilant about Britain and whimsical outside the pub

indicators.note: about means the word for vigilant goes round the letter for Britain

parts.note: vigilant means alert

indicators.note: outside means the word for whimsical wraps round the word for the pub

parts.note: fey can mean whimsical or otherworldly
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An actor played Churchill as watchful over Britain and fanciful outside the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor starred as Winston Churchill in the 2002 film The Gathering Storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The English actor won an Emmy for playing Winston Churchill in the television film The Gathering Storm.

clue.text: Avoid rascal, no-good neighbours, or tie nasty restrictions on them

indicators.note: nasty means the letters are treated roughly and mixed up
no-good means the letter for good is removed from the next word

parts.note: G is short for good

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a bad neighbour or impose nasty curbs on such people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-good' drops G (good) from NEIGHBOURS; 'nasty' rearranges that with AVOID, RASCAL, OR and TIE. ASBOs were British court orders curbing nuisance behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Such orders were British civil court restrictions placed on people causing nuisance to neighbours.

clue.text: Drake, or hen sadly in depth, at sea in this!

definitions.text: Drake, or hen sadly in depth, at sea in this!

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of the bird are rearranged in distress

explanation.surface: A duck, drake or hen, is out of its depth on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drake' looks like a male duck, and 'hen' its mate, but Sir Francis Drake sailed round the world in this ship. 'sadly' rearranges HEN as ENH.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake circumnavigated the globe in his galleon of that name in 1577 to 1580.

clue.text: Gaslight

parts.note: read as a gas giving light, as in a glowing advertising sign tube, rather than an old street lamp

explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas glows red-orange in electric signs, so it is literally a gas that gives light.

clue.text: Sharp as wine with added peel, say

definitions.meaning: sharp in taste, harsh or biting

definitions.text: as wine with added peel, say
definitions.meaning: wine with citrus peel added would have a puckering, tannic dryness

explanation.surface: A drink described as tart, like wine with zest in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent taste is sharp and puckering, as citrus peel would make a wine.

clue.text: Eccentric chap, one supported by a restored monarchy

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the earlier letters sit above the next one

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, a disc on a shaft turning off-centre
bod is slang for a chap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An odd fellow is propped up by a reinstated monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective for chap, but it is a noun: a cam in engineering. Cambodia's monarchy was restored in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia abolished its monarchy in 1970 and restored King Sihanouk to the throne in 1993.

clue.text: Rope tricks originating in this pot?

definitions.text: Rope tricks originating in this pot?

parts.words: Rope tricks originating in this pot?
parts.note: plays on the Indian rope trick, on rope made from a fibre plant, and on pot as slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Did magicians' rope tricks come from a pot?
explanation.definitionFit: The cannabis plant gives both rope fibre and the drug called pot, and the famous rope trick is Indian.

clue.text: Pet guinea pig, they say, stood guard

parts.note: a pet is an animal kept, so pet suggests the word kept

indicators.note: they say means the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig

explanation.surface: A pet guinea pig stood sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: To keep cave (Latin 'beware', said KAY-vee) is British school slang for keeping lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping watch for teachers in British school slang was called keeping cave, from the Latin for beware.

clue.text: Surely what solvers do when going to the dogs

definitions.text: what solvers do when going to the dogs
definitions.meaning: readers at the greyhound track would place wagers

explanation.surface: Certainly, solvers gamble when they visit the greyhound track.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal emphatic certainly, and literally describes the reader wagering at the races.

clue.text: Clouding stink over knight with general rejoicing losing head

indicators.note: over means the word for stink is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a stink
N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: jubilation is general rejoicing

explanation.surface: Smell drifts over a knight as the crowd celebrates, obscuring things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BO to OB; 'losing head' removes J from JUBILATION. 'general' looks like an army officer but just means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnubilation is a rare word for clouding over, or the dimming of the mind.

clue.text: See 19 across
Being an ascetic Jew, not born in France

indicators.note: not means the following French word is taken out

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect
French for born is ne

explanation.surface: Being an ascetic Jew who was not born in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes NE (French né, born) from ESSENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is Latin for to be, used in English philosophy for existence or essential nature.

clue.text: Long story, one having cover with adult content

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: with adult content means the letter for adult forms the filling

parts.note: a lid is a cover
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A long tale, kept under cover, with adult material inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adult content' suggests racy material; here A is the content of LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is the classic long narrative, and the word now means any lengthy tale.

clue.text: Down-and-out wrapped in lots of paper with bottles

indicators.note: wrapped in means one word is enclosed by the other

parts.note: reams are large quantities of paper
a hobo is a down-and-out

explanation.surface: A tramp sleeps wrapped in newspaper beside his bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: A rehoboam is a large wine bottle holding six standard bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehoboams are big champagne bottles, each holding about four and a half litres.

clue.text: So Croesus was with lady in distress

indicators.note: distress means the letters are troubled and scrambled

explanation.surface: The rich king Croesus was with a lady in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges LADY and IN. Croesus was the wealthy king of Lydia.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus ruled Lydia in Asia Minor, so he was Lydian by nationality.

clue.text: A literary trio swapping lines for note, so to speak

indicators.note: swapping means one set of letters is exchanged for another

parts.note: the Sitwells, Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell, were a literary family trio
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A trio of writers exchange lines for a musical note, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping' replaces LL (lines) in SITWELL with RE (a note), giving SITWERE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock qualifier meaning in a manner of speaking.
